about.title: about
about.paragraph_1: the viewer stands before a gigantic “do not look” sign, yet there is nothing else to see—the sign itself is the only content. the secret is that there is no secret. the crossed-out eye, normally a small interface icon warning of “sensitive” content, grows here to monumental scale. the prohibition sign leaves the interface and occupies physical space. what was meant to protect something from prying eyes becomes an object of universal display. the intimate act of privacy turns into a public memorial.
about.paragraph_2: a total banner filling the entire room transforms it from a passive exhibition hall into an interactive playroom: a gift that cannot be seen.
about.paragraph_3: the rules of this game are paradoxical: the viewer is invited to play hide-and-seek with themself, where there is absolutely nothing to hide or seek. once inside the total sign, a person inevitably begins testing the space, searching for an opening, a trick, or a hidden trigger. the room itself becomes a site for a safe experiment on one’s own curiosity, where prohibition turns into the principal entertainment attraction.
